name: Inductive Reasoning
definition: Uses observed patterns or sampled cases to support a broader conclusion or prediction. The evidence may support the conclusion strongly, but does not logically guarantee it.

name: Deductive Reasoning
definition: Presents a conclusion as following necessarily from premises. A valid deduction cannot have true premises and a false conclusion; an invalid deduction fails that guarantee. Validity alone does not establish that the premises are true.

name: Abductive Reasoning
definition: Proposes a plausible best explanation for observations. The explanation can be revised when new evidence appears; it is not guaranteed simply because it fits the observations.
